---
title: Employee CLI recovery
description: Operation-scoped employee CREATE recovery with existing CLI authentication.
updatedAt: "2026-10-21"
audience: developers
---

The operation-only Web route is
`/api/v1/infrastructure/internal-accounts/employees/operations/{operationId}/cli-recovery`.
Its CLI authorization grant is separate from Infrastructure audience acceptance.
It verifies the unchanged CLI access bearer, CLI origin, current required-MFA
policy/lineage and the existing current employee administrator checks. CLI recovery
also requires a valid signed email that canonically matches the freshly read,
confirmed Auth email, including when both addresses are internal. Missing or
invalid email fails closed for reads and writes. Ordinary Infrastructure
authorization keeps its existing behavior. There is
no CLI-to-Infra exchange, actor override, service-auth bypass or ordinary CREATE
admission. The release owner must independently review this grant and require
exact-commit Web build, lint, type-check and test CI before any authorized release.

For repository operator code, load the existing CLI configuration through its
normal loader and create the existing SDK client. Do not print configuration,
headers, passwords or credentials. Recovery requests must use a client without
automatic refresh/replay: a final authorization failure can follow a committed
adjudication or resume. Refresh authentication separately before starting if needed.

```ts
import { TuturuuuUserClient } from '@tuturuuu/sdk';
import {
  inspectEmployeeCliRecovery,
  observeEmployeeCliRecoveryOutcome,
  submitEmployeeCliRecovery,
} from '@tuturuuu/internal-api/infrastructure';
// Repository operator code uses the existing SDK configuration loader.
import { readCliConfig } from '../../packages/sdk/src/cli/config';

const config = await readCliConfig();
if (!config.session?.accessToken || !config.session.expiresAt ||
    config.session.expiresAt * 1000 <= Date.now()) {
  throw new Error('Authenticate with ttr login before recovery');
}
const client = new TuturuuuUserClient({
  baseUrl: config.baseUrl,
  accessToken: config.session.accessToken,
  // Omit refreshToken: this client must not retry a mutation after a 401.
});
const options = client.getClientOptions();
const state = await inspectEmployeeCliRecovery(originalOperationId, options);
```

The caller supplies its retained original operation ID; no production identity is
embedded in the adapter. Independently compare the returned actor and complete
identity tuple to the authorized retained intent. A `fenced`/unavailable response
or an actor mismatch stops the procedure. GET never claims or creates anything.

For `eligible` version 2, the original actor must actually establish terminal
rejection from retained evidence and explicitly approve every existing
attestation. Submit `{ action: 'adjudicate', adjudication }` once with the exact
returned tuple, original lease/attempt, retained event ID and evidence SHA-256.
A nearby provider 422 and account absence do not establish terminal rejection.
After an uncertain response, inspect; do not blindly repeat adjudication.

Only after an independently matching `retry_ready` version-3 readback may the
operator explicitly submit `{ action: 'resume', expected: state,
temporaryPassword }` once through `submitEmployeeCliRecovery`. Obtain the fresh
password privately and keep it transient. The route rechecks current
administrator authorization, operation/key and every identity/audit field before
claiming the original operation. The existing journal reauthorizes its SQL and
provider phases. After all awaited resume work, the route freshly checks the CLI
token, MFA and current administrator authority before disclosing any result.
Authorization loss withholds the result and returns `nextAction: inspect`; the
mutation may already have committed. Retain the original operation and evidence,
restore authorization separately, and inspect without replaying the mutation.
The typed client accepts adjudication only at HTTP 200, and resume only as HTTP
201/created, 202/pending or 409/conflict with the matching original identity.
Contradictory HTTP/payload pairs require inspection and never establish completion.
An uncertain CREATE returns inspection guidance, never permission
for another CREATE or replacement UUID. Use the same unexpired CLI access
credential for read-only original-operation outcome observation:

```ts
const outcome = await observeEmployeeCliRecoveryOutcome({
  operationId: originalOperationId,
  targetUserId: retainedOriginalTargetUserId,
  email: retainedOriginalEmail,
  displayName: retainedOriginalDisplayName,
}, options);
```

This calls `GET .../cli-recovery?view=outcome` with the original operation key.
Default GET remains rejection inspection and fences pending/active phases;
`view=outcome` uses the normal observation factory with fresh CLI authorization,
original actor/operation binding, independent provider identity, fresh SQL proof
and final authorization before disclosure. It never claims, creates, provisions,
unbans or replays. It requires no Infrastructure audience or credential exchange.
Only HTTP 200/created or stopped and 202/pending are valid outcome pairs; conflict,
contradictory statuses, identity mismatches and errors never establish completion.
The original target, email and creation name remain bound; when terminal active
SQL provenance supplies `creationDisplayName`, that immutable name binds the
operation while `displayName` reports the current managed profile name.
POST resume still requires the exact `retry_ready` version-3 tuple. Authentication
restoration happens separately; do not add SDK refresh/replay to these calls.

Synthetic local regressions cover signed credential target/scope/origin, expiry,
refresh/signature failures, stale/missing signed or current emails, authorization
changes during awaited journal work, the HTTP/outcome matrix, owned/missing/foreign
operations, tuple/version changes, lost acknowledgement and no CREATE during
adjudication. `employee-cli-outcome-route.test.ts` exercises the actual GET with
signed CLI credentials, foreign actor/operation, active/pending/stopped, provider
ban, contradictory fresh SQL, stale authority and no mutation dispatch.
`employee-cli-outcome.test.ts` covers identity and the strict read-only HTTP matrix
with one dispatch. These tests do not prove production operation state, original actor,
provider effects or delivery. Parent/release custody retains those actions.
